question: Who among the following established the Brahmo Samaj in 1828?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** established the **Brahmo Samaj in 1828** in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was a **social and religious reform movement** in India during the 19th century, aimed at eradicating social evils such as caste discrimination, sati, and child marriage.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often referred to as the **"Father of Modern India"** due to his contributions to social reform and modernization.
 
• He advocated for the **abolition of sati** (the practice of widow self-immolation) and worked with the British government to ensure its legal prohibition in 1829.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was based on the **principles of monotheism** and rejected idol worship, rituals, and the caste system, promoting rationality and individualism instead.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy also emphasized the **importance of education** and the empowerment of women, advocating for women's rights, including the right to property and education.
 
• He played a significant role in introducing **Western education** and modern scientific approaches to Indian society.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj became a platform for discussing social reform and spreading ideas of **liberal thought and rationalism** in Indian society.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**

 
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** (1772–1833) was a prominent social reformer and thinker of the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He was fluent in several languages, including **Bengali, Sanskrit, Persian, Arabic, and English**, which enabled him to study various religious and philosophical texts.
 
• Roy was instrumental in modernizing Indian society by introducing **Western ideals of democracy, liberty, and equality**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Brahmo Samaj:**
 
 
• The Brahmo Samaj promoted the idea of **universal brotherhood** and sought to eliminate caste and gender discrimination in Indian society.
 
• It opposed superstitions, meaningless rituals, and idol worship, focusing on **rationality and ethical living**.
 
• The movement laid the foundation for many subsequent reform movements in India, including those led by **Swami Vivekananda** and **Ramakrishna Paramhansa**.
 
 
 
• **Other Reform Movements:**
 
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy also collaborated with the British government to legalize the **Abolition of Sati (1829)**, marking a significant achievement in his reformist journey.
 
• He was a supporter of the **freedom of press** and established the **Sambad Kaumudi**, a weekly newspaper that raised awareness about social and political issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Swami Dayananda Saraswati:**

 
 
• He founded the **Arya Samaj** in 1875, which also focused on social reform but emphasized Vedic traditions and values.
 
 
 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen:**
 
 
• He was a prominent leader of the **Brahmo Samaj** but joined later and introduced several reforms within the movement.
 
 
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**
 
 
• A contemporary of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, he worked for **widow remarriage** and women's education but was not associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
